reason: Reviewed all five surfaces for the Codex session-handler check. Lifecycle hooks: a new Codex install no longer appends --integration-revision to its commands; an existing install keeps the revision it carries, so every approved handler keeps its exact bytes (tested), and the Codex SessionStart now also records a fingerprint per Notifai handler in session state; hook output is unchanged and the other harnesses keep the per-definition revision. CLI readiness: update --resume no longer reports a changed Codex definition done for a session that started before it; its pending action names the handlers that session lacks and says a new Codex session picks them up (reproduced first as a failing test). doctor adds a 'hooks (session handlers)' row with the same sentence, a gap only when a missing handler serves turn end, the tool boundary or question cards (with the fresh-session user_action), report-only otherwise; for other harnesses it reports the existing 'changed definition has not been observed' line when a callback carried an older revision. doctor's and resume's Codex trust now come from Codex's app-server hooks/list where codex answers, else config.toml as before (one private stdio codex app-server per run, initialized with the shared non-originating client identity, so it claims no originator); ask readiness is unchanged. Notifai skill: references/updates.md (Harness differences) and references/harness-codex.md (After a Notifai update) now say Codex records the handlers a session loaded, that resume and doctor name the missing ones, that a new Codex session picks them up, and that only a feature's handler blocks. Harness setup: unchanged. Domain terms: unchanged. skills/guidance-changes.json carries one new release note for this change.
